observation: Tor 15.0.24 is raw+host-static accepted with targetSdk35; ExpressVPN 12.80.1 is raw+package-level blackbox+host-static accepted with targetSdk37. Both have cold_start_delta=0; neither has install/start evidence. ExpressVPN targetSdk37 exceeds AOSP16 API36 but does not imply install failure.
one_improvement: Add a version-scope label to 200-APK scheduling records: compare exact APK targetSdk to platform API and label within-ceiling, above-ceiling risk, or metadata gap; all remain runtime-unproven until an exact device receipt overrides the label. The label influences review priority only, never raw/static/blackbox admission or an install verdict.
pilot_result: Five offline cases passed: Tor target35 is within-ceiling but unproven; Express target37 is risk but unproven; synthetic target37 with explicit device PASS remains PASS; target35 without device does not auto-PASS; missing target does not auto-FAIL.
counterexample: A future exact targetSdk37 APK may install and cold-start successfully; the rule must preserve that possibility and replace risk label only with actual exact device receipt.
promotion_gate: Candidate only. Peer review exact inputs/labels, then trial on one small mixed-SDK scheduling batch with immutable pre/post queue and exact device outcomes. Adopt only if it prevents misleading install-failure claims without starving above-ceiling samples or delaying independent host scans.
limits: This pilot validates claim discipline, not startup prediction or improved 200-APK throughput. No device action or queue edit was performed.
